items.summary: At Oxford Union in Hamilton, Canada, Qatar's Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani proposed on Friday a new label for small states that have turned size into an advantage. He called them 'Thriving States,' describing them as agile, stable and trusted nations positioned to help build what he termed a 'supply chain of peace.'
items.title: Qatar's Foreign Minister Proposes 'Thriving States' Peace Bloc

items.summary: As India observes Diwali, the Bharat Agriculture Conference 2026 is set for November 11 and 12 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Themed 'Smart Kisan for Viksit Bharat', it features a session with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Presented by Mahindra Tractors and co-presented by Mahadhan Agritech, the event highlights farmers' spirit during the festival.
items.title: Bharat Agriculture Conference Opens in New Delhi During Diwali

items.summary: Tests of petrol samples from Karnataka found ethanol blending levels reaching up to 31.2 percent, surpassing the mandated limit of 20 percent. Leading oil firms including Indian Oil Corporation and Shell are under scrutiny after most tested samples showed excess blending. Concerns focus on fuel efficiency, engine damage, and unclear ethanol content information at stations, prompting calls for government action against non-compliant companies.
items.title: Karnataka Petrol Tests Reveal Ethanol Blending Above Mandate

items.summary: As Deepawali approaches, The Federal examines whether past wrongs can be righted through apologies and reparations. King Charles III expressed horror at the transatlantic slave trade but declined a formal apology. Shashi Tharoor argues British colonial rule collapsed India's share of global GDP from nearly 27% to less than 3%, while up to 3 million people died in the Bengal Famine of 1943, exacerbated by Winston Churchill's grain diversion policy. Columnist Minhaz Merchant estimated British exploitation at US$ 500 billion as of 1988, which he speculates would exceed US$ 6 trillion today. Meanwhile, Britain paid roughly 20 million to compensate former slave owners under the 1833 Slavery Abolition Act while giving nothing to enslaved people. Nations like Australia and Germany have issued apologies or compensation, yet The Federal notes opinions are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect its views.
items.title: Ethics and Precedents of Historical Reparations

items.summary: As Sen. Alan Armstrong of Oklahoma prepares to leave office, a bipartisan permitting bill slated for its first vote next week could advance his priority and benefit the Williams Companies, where he served as chief executive and chairman for 15 years until March. The legislation would restrict states' ability to deny or condition water quality certifications under Section 401 of the Clean Water Act—changes environmental lawyers say appear tailored to a small number of Northeast gas pipeline projects, including the disputed Constitution pipeline Williams has sought through New York for over a decade. Armstrong held tens of millions in Williams stock and hired former colleagues amid conflict-of-interest concerns; his office declined comment while ethics watchdogs questioned whether he violated rules. Environmental groups argue the bill taints negotiations and favors fossil fuels.
items.title: Oklahoma Senator's Pipeline Bill Would Benefit His Former Company

items.summary: Southern Railway's General Manager Subba Rao said the railway will ensure comfortable travel for pilgrims attending the 2028 Mahamaham festival at Kumbakonam. Around 25 lakh pilgrims are expected to arrive by rail, prompting station development and added facilities including lifts. Work is underway on doubling a 30 km track section from Sundaraperumal Koil to Aduthurai to enable more trains, though the Thanjavur–Villupuram line doubling remains incomplete.
items.title: Southern Railway Plans Comfortable Journey for Mahamaham Pilgrims

items.summary: Analysts told CNA that Singapore banks may confront a more difficult environment in 2027 despite higher interest rates. DBS and UOB missed analysts' expectations for the third quarter, while OCBC's net profit grew 3 per cent to S$2.04 billion, beating estimates. Eric Xiao of CMC Markets said wealth fees fell 6 per cent at DBS as clients traded less. Ritesh Ganeriwal of Syfe noted interest rates were no longer doing the heavy lifting and margins are being squeezed. Joanna Cheah of Jefferies described earnings drivers as increasingly differentiated between lenders, with UOB facing greater net interest margin pressure while DBS and OCBC saw recovery in late Q3.
items.title: Singapore banks face tougher outlook in 2027 amid mixed Q3 results

items.summary: A blast struck the Vasundhara police outpost under Indirapuram police station in Ghaziabad late Friday night, damaging window panes. A food delivery person present there sustained minor injuries. On Saturday, police said authorities rushed Anti-Terrorist Squad and bomb disposal teams to the site. ACP Suryabali Maurya stated that the exact nature of the object causing the explosion would be determined after an investigation.
items.title: Blast at Ghaziabad Police Outpost Injures Delivery Worker, Triggers ATS Response

items.summary: Sreeja Reddy Koya, a 23-year-old student at UMass Boston from Nalgonda district, Telangana, has been missing since November 2 after going for a walk. Her father Yadagiri Reddy says her phone remained switched off. State Roads and Buildings Minister Komatireddy Venkat Reddy urged the Consulate General of India in Boston, the External Affairs Ministry, and the Boston Police Department to help trace her.
items.title: Telangana Student Missing in US as Family Seeks Help

items.summary: An explosion occurred Friday night inside a police outpost in Vasundhara, Indirapuram, Ghaziabad, injuring a delivery worker after shattered glass struck him. ACP Suryabali Maurya said the sub-inspector and delivery boy were present when it happened; only Maurya is named as speaking for police. On Saturday officials inspected the site while an investigation runs to identify what caused the blast. Police say the object responsible will be known only after a detailed probe, and further details are awaited.
items.title: Delivery Worker Injured in Ghaziabad Police Outpost Explosion

items.summary: Progressive Jane Kim won California’s insurance commissioner race, campaigning on a state-run single-payer program covering homeowners against wildfire damage pending legislative and gubernatorial approval. Her plan would draw from existing wildfire premiums with rebuild caps; critics warn of cost burden and no prior model.
items.title: California Voters Back Single-Payer Wildfire Insurance Plan

items.summary: Air quality in Delhi remained 'Very Poor' before Diwali, with the city's average AQI at 366 and readings crossing the 400 mark at 22 locations placed in the Severe category. IIT recorded the highest reading at 442, followed by Punjabi Bagh (433) and Vivek Vihar (427). Levels showed little improvement even after GRAP Stage-III restrictions took effect across Delhi and adjoining Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan districts ahead of Diwali.
items.title: Delhi Air Quality Stays Very Poor Before Diwali as GRAP Stage III Invoked

items.summary: The item is a single-sentence caption identifying an editorial cartoon by Martin Rowson, titled 'on the aftermath of the US midterm elections.' No figures, dates, or direct statements are given. The only location named in the text is the United States.
items.title: Martin Rowson cartoon on US midterm election aftermath

items.summary: Global tech stocks fell sharply following the Democratic Party's victory in the US midterm elections, with concerns that artificial intelligence development could slow. Major companies including Apple, Tesla and Nvidia together lost about $1tn during one trading session. The drop raises questions over whether it reflects market volatility or a warning sign before an AI bubble bursts.
items.title: Tech stocks plunge after Democrats win US midterms, AI bubble fears rise

items.summary: Hyundai's larger three-row electric SUV, the IONIQ 9, now appears to be a stronger lease deal than its smaller sibling. The base IONIQ 5 SE Standard Range leases from $359 a month over 24 months with $4,999 due at signing for an effective cost of $567 per month, while the extended-range version runs $577 monthly. Hyundai's larger IONIQ 9 starts around $58,955 to buy but leases from $419 a month over 36 months with $4,999 down for an effective cost of $557 per month. The comparison notes the IONIQ 9 offers more range and seating space than the midsize IONIQ 5.
items.title: IONIQ 9 Lease Beats Smaller IONIQ 5 on Effective Cost

items.summary: Loggerhead sea turtles are expanding their nesting range westward across the Mediterranean, from Italy toward Spain and France, researchers say. Sandra Hochscheid of the Stazione Zoologica Anton Dohrn in Naples describes it as a real-time population expansion along previously uncolonized coasts. She attributes rising juvenile growth to warming seas that let turtles reach sexual maturity earlier than before. The shift brings conflict with heavily developed beaches: nearly 27,000 private beach clubs cover about 43% of Italy’s coastline, and light pollution exposed 87% of nests in Campania in 2022-2023, requiring human intervention for 82% of surveyed nests. Conservation groups like Legambiente’s Life Turtlenest project now work with local operators to install low-intensity lighting; mandatory compliance begins in 2027.
items.title: Loggerhead Turtles Expand Mediterranean Nesting Range Westward

items.summary: In an interview with Talking Europe, EU's former top diplomat Josep Borrell reacts to the Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections. He warns that President Donald Trump is still "a very dangerous person for the world." Despite the election result, Borrell says Trump retains veto powers and remains a threat.
items.title: Borrell Warns Trump Remains Dangerous for World After US Midterms

items.summary: The IEA’s India Renewable Energy Market Report 2026, launched at the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit in New Delhi, expects India’s installed solar PV capacity to exceed 350 GW by 2030. Total renewable power could reach around 530 GW, with wind near 90 GW and hydropower at 75 GW. The path includes rooftop schemes like PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana and corporate procurement; sustained expansion would need faster grid, storage and flexibility investment.
items.title: IEA Forecasts India Solar Capacity Surpassing 350 GW by 2030

items.summary: According to a US intelligence memo cited by the Financial Times, American officials believe Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang (Huang Le), an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed suspected of spying for China. The findings predate Trump's Beijing summit and follow New York Times reporting on surveillance linking her to information passing to Beijing amid chip-export scrutiny. Nvidia declined to comment, while the company said it had already debunked smuggling claims; China dismissed the accusations as groundless smears.
items.title: US Intelligence Memo Alleges Nvidia CEO's Romantic Ties to Chinese Spy

items.summary: NetLink NBN Trust named former ST Engineering and Singtel executive Low Ka Hoe as its CEO-designate, succeeding Tong Yew Heng effective Nov 10. A bourse filing dated Nov 6 states he will take over on Apr 1, 2027, when he also joins the manager's board as an executive director. The trustee-manager added that NetLink posted a distribution per unit of $0.0274 for its first half ended Sep 30, up 1.1% from a year earlier; units closed flat at $0.94 on Friday. Derryn Wong reported the item in THE BUSINESS TIMES.
items.title: Low Ka Hoe Named NetLink NBN Trust CEO-Successor

items.summary: Schroders is selling Wisteria Mall in Yishun, northern Singapore, through brokers Knight Frank and Savills to raise around $220 million. The exercise closes late November. Schroders acquired the London-based asset manager by Nuveen in October and bought the mall for $208 million in 2022; it is now about 93% occupied. A spokesperson said the firm regularly reviews its real estate portfolios to serve investors.
items.title: Schroders Lists Singapore Mall in Property Offload Push

items.summary: A Financial Times report citing unnamed officials says a US intelligence memo from early 2026 alleged that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, suspected of working for China's Ministry of State Security. The claims follow earlier reporting on surveillance and photos. Nvidia called the interactions routine business meetings; China dismissed them as groundless speculation. No public charges exist against either person.
items.title: Nvidia, China and US Officials Reject Alleged Spy Operation Tied to Jensen Huang

items.summary: CGTN Digital journalist Shen Shiwei interviewed CEOs from the US, Germany and Switzerland, plus a Moldovan official, about their selections at the 9th China International Import Expo in Shanghai. The leaders highlighted products prioritizing innovation, high technology, low carbon output, eco-friendliness and user orientation, with China's 15th Five-Year Plan among the topics of focus.
items.title: Global CEOs Share Top Picks at CIIE

items.summary: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee accused the BJP of disrupting traditional Kali Puja celebrations after an alleged attack on Trinamool Congress general secretary Abhishek Banerjee's residence. In a statement, she asked why attackers came at 3:00 in the morning with a gang of thugs if they had the courage to use a bulldozer. Abhishek claimed the incident followed reconnaissance and called it his seventh attempt on his life.
items.title: Mamata Banerjee Condemns Attack on Abhishek Banerjee Ahead of Kali Puja

items.summary: Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge accused the Central government of misleading people about ethanol content in E20 petrol, citing NABL-accredited laboratory reports he said showed blending up to 35-40 per cent against announced limits. He alleged the programme benefits companies linked to Union ministers and called it an experiment on India's population. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi separately claimed samples from seven Karnataka districts exceeded 20 per cent ethanol. State-run oil marketing companies IOC, BPCL and HPCL disputed both findings, saying their fuel meets IS 17021 specifications of 19-21 per cent and questioning the sampling procedures.
items.title: Karnataka minister alleges Centre is over-blending ethanol in E20 petrol

items.summary: China delivered its latest financial work report, presented by central bank Governor Pan Gongsheng to the NPC Standing Committee. The report shows local government financing vehicle debt fell 92% from March 2023 levels, with operational debt down 79%, and approved over 8.4 trillion yuan of real estate loans. Deputies flagged lingering risks while calling for market stabilization measures and deeper opening-up. New corporate loan rates reached a historic low of 2.96%. The report sets five priorities centered on supportive monetary policy and no systemic risk.
items.title: NPC Deputies Urge Market Stability and Financial Opening-Up in China's Work Report

items.summary: House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries promises to stop tariffs raising American prices, while incoming Senate Finance Committee chairman Ron Wyden says he will reassert congressional authority over trade policy. Even Republican Senator Ted Cruz called tariffs too expensive. Lawmakers warn curbing President Donald Trump's tariff powers may be difficult and could trigger infighting in both parties as new duties loom.
items.title: Democrats Vow to Challenge Trump Tariffs Over Rising Costs

items.summary: In Nelson, Blair Cameron leads by 878 votes with 72% of the vote counted, a margin under 1000 still seen as tight. Winston Peters urged calm until all facts are known. Projected seat counts show National at 42 and Labour at 35 in a shifting parliament.
items.title: NZ Election Count Tight in Nelson as Labour Levels With National

items.summary: A spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in the UK said China strongly opposed a joint statement from the UK, United States, Canada and Australia commenting on anti-China figure Joshua Wong Chi-fung's sentencing by the Hong Kong High Court. The remarks were described as unwarranted interference in Hong Kong affairs. Beijing urged the UK to stop interfering under any pretext.
items.title: China Condemns UK and Allies Over Joshua Wong Sentencing Remarks

items.summary: A Beijing laboratory reports that DREADDs, a neurostimulation method previously used only on animals, reduced seizures by an average of 92.6% in three drug-resistant epilepsy patients (s4). The approach uses a genetically-engineered virus to alter brain receptors and clozapine to switch targeted regions off (s5-s6), with adverse events rated mild-to-moderate (grade 1 or 2) (s6). At the NIH BRAIN Initiative meeting in Bethesda, inventor Professor Brian Roth noted at least seven registered Chinese DREADDs trials (s8). Cambridge's Ewan St John-Smith called it exciting but questioned readiness and flagged viral-delivery risks (s10-s22), while others see China reshaping neuroscience leadership (s26-s30)
items.title: China Reports Early Success in Human DREADDs Trials for Epilepsy

items.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India recorded its highest-ever Electronic Gold Receipts trading volume, with festive-period activity reaching 2,27,692 units according to the exchange. NSE Chief Business Development Officer Sriram Krishnan said the record reflects growing acceptance of regulated gold ownership and could help mobilise domestic recycled gold while potentially reducing import dependence.
items.title: NSE EGR Trading Hits Record on Dhanteras

items.summary: Seven experts offered views on buying gold and silver ahead of the festival, warning that near-term volatility, rising interest rates and inflation could pressure prices. Abhisek Bahinipati of Invesco Mutual Fund suggested a 15% allocation to precious metals for most investors, with roughly two-thirds in gold and one-third in silver. Others cautioned against chasing recent gains or deploying full amounts at once, favouring staggered buying. Motilal Oswal Private Wealth kept its outlook neutral amid higher yields, while Nuvama flagged that sharp corrections could redirect liquidity toward equities.
items.title: Experts weigh in on gold and silver investing this Diwali

items.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India detailed changes in two circulars issued on November 6, covering the closing price discovery mechanism for eligible equity securities, derivatives trading hours and futures settlement prices. The revisions follow a Securities and Exchange Board of India circular dated October 15, 2026. Most provisions take effect from December 7, 2026, while changes to unexecuted limit and disclosed quantity orders begin February 8, 2027.
items.title: NSE Overhauls Closing Price Discovery and Derivatives Rules from December

items.summary: Santos FC announced on Friday that it has appointed Neymar's father and agent, Neymar Sr., as its chief executive. His agency NR Sports holds the rights to his son's name and image, and he reportedly played a key role in Neymar's career. According to Brazilian media reports, his contract runs until December and depends on president Marcelo Teixeira being re-elected next month.
items.title: Neymar Sr Appointed CEO of Santos FC

items.summary: The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has invited applications from DPIIT-registered startups in film and allied technologies to participate in the WaveX Startup Pavilion at WAVES Bazaar during the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) Goa 2026, which will be held from November 20 to 28. The initiative aims to give innovative startups a platform to showcase products, technologies and solutions to national and international film and media industry participants while enabling networking with filmmakers, production houses and investors. Eligible applicants are screened by a Selection Committee constituted by WaveX, the Ministry's startup accelerator for the Media and Entertainment sector.
items.title: I&B Ministry Opens Startup Applications for WAVES Bazaar Film Pavilion at IFFI Goa 2026

items.summary: The author spent two years comparing manual heating control with an AI system, Tado X, in a 1930s solid-brick house. After controlling for hot water usage across the same 213 days from November to May and similar outside temperatures, the AI-controlled heating used 11,735.7 kWh of gas versus 14,316.7 kWh manually — a reduction of about 18%, or 2,581 kWh less. At the current energy price cap ending 31 December, that equates to £205.70 saved. The author notes savings could be larger for less frugal households and highlights comfort benefits beyond efficiency.
items.title: A Two-Year Test of AI Heating Controls

items.summary: Early release prisoners in England and Wales risk being released into street homelessness as temporary probation accommodation expires, according to charities and probation staff. James, a 37-year-old released from prison in August with two electronic tags, said he has nowhere to go after his Somerset housing was rejected. Tania Bassett of Napo called it a
items.title: Probation staff warn early releases face street homelessness

items.summary: Nationwide building society launched a fixed-rate Member Exclusive Bond paying 5.3% interest, available to its more than 19 million members with deposits of £1 to £10,000. A full £10,000 deposit earns £1,381 over the 30-month term. The launch follows a Bank of England base rate rise to 4%. Nationwide says it rewards member loyalty; experts expect fixed rates to hold after Thursday's hike.
items.title: Nationwide Launches Fixed-Rate Savings Account at Market-Leading Rate

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV, aged 71 and three weeks post lung-cancer surgery, told reporters he is “in pretty good health” as his 12-day tour began in Montevideo, Uruguay. He praised the medical staff and said doctors report the cancer has not spread. On arrival crowds greeted him; later he urged universal healthcare to be accessible to everyone.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV opens Latin America tour in good health

items.summary: Over the five trading sessions ending November 6, the Sensex rose 8.82%, or 6,568 points, to close at 81,028, gaining each session. Amid this broad-based rally, around 45 stocks from the BSE 200 index advanced in all five consecutive sessions from November 2 to 6. From these, nine were shortlisted for consistent gains throughout the period, delivering cumulative returns ranging from 15% to 20%. Data source: ACE Equity.
items.title: Nine Stocks Gained for Five Days in a Row on Sensex Rally

items.summary: France faces mounting debt costs amid nationwide protests and a government lacking parliamentary majority. Public debt stands at around 120% of GDP, roughly double Germany's ~65%, while France carries negative credit outlooks and pays nearly 1.6 percentage points more in interest on 10-year bonds than Berlin. The spread over German bonds has doubled since June 2026. Economist Friedrich Heinemann warns rising spreads could trigger a financial crisis unless course changes occur. Researchers note many citizens remain insulated from debt consequences, sustaining political support for costly promises from both far-right and far-left parties.
items.title: France's Rising Debt Costs Threaten Stability Amid Protests

items.summary: Stock exchanges BSE and NSE are set to hold the Muhurat Trading session from 2.20 pm to 3.30 pm on Sunday, marking an age-old Diwali tradition tied to Lakshmi Puja and the start of Samvat 2083. The one-hour session follows a week in which Sensex surged 6,569 points while Nifty rallied nearly 9%, adding about Rs 29 lakh crore to BSE market capitalisation above Rs 500 lakh crore. Analysts advise selective, quality-first investing rather than chasing momentum, noting the limited participation of such sessions. SBI Securities outlines technical levels for Nifty around 24,830-24,850 support and 25,150-25,180 resistance.
items.title: BSE and NSE Set for Muhurat Trading Session on Sunday

items.summary: Moscow carried out missile strikes on Kyiv and the surrounding region overnight Friday to Saturday, targeting energy infrastructure and killing at least one person while injuring eight, authorities said. Russian forces launched attacks damaging a major bridge across the Dnipro River, with explosions rocking the city as ballistic missiles hit the Northern Bridge.
items.title: Russia strikes Kyiv and surrounding region in massive overnight strike

items.summary: Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, six-year-old pandas from China's Chengdu, made their first public appearance at Zoo Atlanta on Friday as visitors queued to see them. The pair arrived September 27 after a decades-long loan arrangement ended amid strained US-China ties. Their return follows a renewed 10-year agreement following a Washington summit between President Trump and Xi Jinping.
items.title: Two Giant Pandas Make Public Debut at Zoo Atlanta

items.summary: Early results from New Zealand's general election show a neck-and-neck race between the Labour Party and National Party-led right-wing coalition after a campaign centred on cost of living. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon faces main challenger Chris Hipkins as polls close. Labour leads at 29.71% versus National's 29.41%, with just over 42% counted, though none are expected to secure a parliamentary majority.
items.title: New Zealand Counting Votes in a Close Election

items.summary: Lupovis, a cybersecurity firm led by CEO Xavier Bellekens, says it detected hackers probing internet-connected refrigeration systems across Europe in the days before supermarket and blood bank cyberattacks on 2 and 3 November. The company observed over 276 attempts from 91 threat actors targeting Danfoss’s AK-SM system manager during a 10-day reconnaissance period peaking on 26 October, suggesting a coordinated operation rather than a lone actor. Lupovis declined to confirm Russia as the culprit, noting servers’ locations do not prove nationality. Experts warn similar weaknesses could affect heating, access control and other building systems, though no ransom or claim of responsibility has emerged.
items.title: Cybersecurity firm traces fridge probes ahead of European attacks

items.summary: CNA reported that SMRT is trialling a new escalator etiquette at City Hall and Raffles Place MRT stations, encouraging commuters to stand on both sides instead of keeping left. Observations found walking up the right side took about 20 seconds versus about 30 seconds for standing still on the left, yet most passengers kept old habits. SMRT Trains president Lam Sheau Kai said the month-long trial aims to improve safety and capacity. Interviews with 10 commuters showed strong attachment to keeping left, though some acknowledged exceptions for elderly or less steady riders. Similar moves in London reportedly increased capacity by about 30 per cent, while South Korean studies cited higher wear on one side of escalators.
items.title: Singapore Commuters Resist Escalator Stand-BOTH-Sides Trial

items.summary: The Gurugram district administration issued show-cause notices to private commercial establishments, including the law firms Trilegal and JSA Advocates & Solicitors on Golf Course Road, after inspections found them exceeding a 50% physical office attendance limit. The mandate was set by Deputy Commissioner Uttam Singh following directions from the Commission for Air Quality Management amid worsening air quality in Delhi-NCR between 5 and 20 November. Inspections reportedly showed JSA with around 87 of 117 employees present, against a permitted limit of about 58, and Trilegal with around 160 of 262 staff, versus roughly 131 allowed. Firms were given 24 hours to respond or face proceedings under the CAQM Act 2021; Singh said monitoring would continue.
items.title: Gurugram Law Firms Cited for Breaching Work-From-Home Pollution Rule

items.summary: A research team from Soochow University in China developed a portable solar-powered device that produces drinking water from turbid, saline, oily and highly acidic sources. The prototype produced 1. 64 liters of clean water in eight hours using an evaporation surface measuring just 30. 72 cm². It combines foldable solar cells with a Fresnel lens to concentrate sunlight onto the surface without grid or fuel supply. Outdoor tests were conducted on selected days in January and February 2025, achieving apparent energy efficiency of 93. 31% and production rate of 69. 46 liters per square meter per hour.
items.title: Soochow University Team Unveils Portable Solar Watermaker

items.summary: Three state-run oil marketing companies—Indian Oil, Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum—rejected Karnataka's claim that petrol at some outlets contained ethanol above the 20% limit. The government said 11 of 14 samples from seven districts exceeded the threshold, with the highest concentration recorded in an IOCL sample. The OMCs disputed the sampling exercise conducted without their representatives and questioned whether certificates specified the required technical standards. They cited a joint quality-monitoring exercise testing all E20 samples within the prescribed range across 27 states and Union territories.
items.title: Karnataka OMCs Reject Ethanol Blending Claims

items.summary: Stacey Waaka scored three tries as New Zealand beat Fetu Samoa in the women's Rugby League World Cup semifinal, reaching a seventh consecutive decider. The win capped her tournament of six tries and made New Zealand the only nation to reach every final since 2000. Waaka said: 'I can't wait for this next week.'
items.title: Waaka hat-trick sends Kiwi Ferns to seventh straight women's Rugby League World Cup final

items.summary: A list of six new nonfiction books is set to be published in November, with all information sourced from the publishers. The selection spans biographies and memoirs: Paul Morley's David Hockney: An Artist for Life; Philip Delves Broughton's Embargo on how the 1973 oil crisis changed the world, more than 50 years later; Dan Jones's Castles: A Fortified History of the World; Ben Dark's Green Kingdom, tracing plant evolution from 484 million years ago through 16 families; Caitlin Moran's How to Be Hopeful; and Elena Dudum's Palestinian memoir They Told Me Back Home Would Be Beautiful.
items.title: Six New Nonfiction Titles for November

items.summary: Environmental groups worldwide are turning to artificial intelligence to analyze climate data, track forest fires and count endangered wildlife – embracing a technology they also warn is driving surges in electricity demand, water use and greenhouse-gas emissions. The contradiction forces these organizations to justify their AI use while fighting the crises it worsens. Groups like Conservation International say AI helps them move faster amid urgent biodiversity threats; Kenya's Save the Elephants cut survey time from nine months to hours. Data-center footprint could more than double by 2030, and global consumption is projected at about 945 terawatt-hours annually – roughly equal to Japan's use. Organizations like Greenpeace push back on new data centers as unnecessary.
items.title: Environmental Groups Adopt AI While Warning of Its Environmental Costs

items.summary: A controversy has emerged in Karnataka over ethanol blending exceeding the mandated 20 percent limit, with fuel samples showing levels as high as 31.2 percent. Tests across seven districts, including Bengaluru, raised safety and vehicle concerns. Indian Oil Corporation Limited denied the claims, citing its own tests within regulated ranges. Major oil companies have proposed joint testing to ensure transparency.
items.title: Karnataka Raises Concerns Over Ethanol Blending Exceeding E20 Limits in Petrol

items.summary: The Arunachal Pradesh government released four protesters opposing the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project from Jully Central Jail near Itanagar on Saturday, nearly a month after their arrest. Detained on October 9 under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 2014, they were freed as a goodwill gesture toward the Siang Indigenous Farmers' Forum. The government said police cases would follow legal process and urged resumed talks with Chief Minister Pema Khandu, while withdrawal of security forces remains pending.
items.title: Arunachal Frees Siang Dam Protesters and Invites Return of Talks

items.summary: A Louisiana divorce dispute over shared property and spending tied to a new partner ended in an appellate reversal. The trial court ordered the wife to pay her former husband $205,000 for mishandling community assets. On appeal, the Third Circuit Court of Appeal rejected key parts of that ruling and instead ordered the husband to pay the wife $176,800. The article notes the reversal reflects errors in how the trial court classified, valued, or allocated property and spending, illustrating that Louisiana divorce judgments are not always final.
items.title: Louisiana Divorce Verdict Reversed on Appeal, Flipping Payment Direction

items.summary: Rakesh Shah of Edelweiss urged the government in a Bloomberg Television interview to consider removing capital gains tax to attract foreign investors. Foreign outflows exceeded $28 billion this year, yet inflows topped $5 billion over three weeks amid domestic recovery. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said she would look at market-related tax changes without confirming specifics.
items.title: Edelweiss Chairman Calls for Scrapping Capital Gains Tax

items.summary: Usman Khawaja has claimed that all members of the Australian cricket team, including support staff, were aware of sandpaper use during the 2018 South Africa tour. His account contradicts Cricket Australia's original investigation, which found only Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft had prior knowledge. They received suspensions ranging from nine to 12 months. Both CA and former coach Darren Lehmann have rejected his allegations.
items.title: Khawaja claims entire Australian team knew of ball-tampering plan

items.summary: Police say a man lured an eight-year-old girl with golgappas, took her to an isolated plot about 500 metres from home, assaulted her and struck her on the head with an iron rod. Her body was recovered around 2am Saturday after it bore injury marks on the head. Police registered a case under sections 103(1) and 238 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita at Sikandrabad station, while teams trace the accused.
items.title: Bulandshahr Man Charged in Rape and Murder of Young Girl

items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi alleged a “deeply sinister plot” after Union minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh announced that voter ID cards, not Aadhaar, would determine eligibility for panchayati raj benefits. The announcement coincided with nationwide protests over an electoral-roll revision during which 13 crore electors were reportedly removed in affected states. Gandhi called the change a theft of rights and accused chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of colluding with the BJP to steal elections; Singh denied distorting facts, saying the shift prevents middlemen from exploiting schemes.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Accuses BJP of Voter-Roll Manipulation and Aadhaar Shift

items.summary: The Israeli army arrested six Palestinians early Saturday during raids across the occupied West Bank, which included home searches, according to local sources. Forces detained five people in Jenin and took them to an undisclosed location; Wafa reported a raid on Askar refugee camp near Nablus that led to one arrest. No arrests were reported in al-Zawiya, Tammun, Iktaba or al-Amari. The army conducts near-daily campaigns targeting men, women and children, often involving assaults and the destruction of household belongings. Around 9,350 Palestinian prisoners are held in Israeli prisons.
items.title: Israeli army raids West Bank, arrests six Palestinians

items.summary: An eight-year-old girl was allegedly raped and murdered on Friday after a man known to her family lured her out of her house under the pretext of treating her to golgappas. The accused, identified as Ravi Kashyap, reportedly took her about 500 metres from home, assaulted her and struck her with an iron rod before fleeing; her body was recovered around 2 am on Saturday. Police registered a case under Sections 103(1) and 238 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita at Sikandrabad police station.
items.title: Eight-Year-Old Girl Murdered in Bulandshahr After Being Lured by Known Man

items.summary: South Australian Police arrested and charged a man with alleged stalking and harassment of the state's lower house Speaker, Nat Cook. The man has been bailed and is scheduled to appear in Christies Beach Magistrates Court on December 7.
items.title: Man Charged With Harassing South Australian Speaker Nat Cook

items.summary: On the eve of Kali Puja, Bengalis observe Bhoot Chaturdashi by lighting fourteen earthen lamps and eating a dish called Choddo Shaak made from fourteen seasonal greens. The night marks remembering departed ancestors and protecting homes from wandering spirits, with popular belief linking it to fourteen generations remembered on this day. Food writer Amit Sen notes the occasion blurs the divide between living and departed people. MasterChef Oindrila Bala compares Bhoot Chaturdashi to Halloween, while food blogger Debjani Roy highlights the greens' health qualities. There is no fixed list of greens; households choose based on local produce and family preference, often avoiding onion and garlic.
items.title: Bengalis Eat Fourteen Seasonal Greens on Bhoot Chaturdashi

items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told CNN that a 'big agreement' voiced by US President Donald Trump to end the Russia-Ukraine war could be dangerous. Published on 07 November 2026, his comments followed Trump's Thursday confirmation of talks with Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev. Zelenskyy said he saw no signals from Moscow and compared any settlement to Yalta, warning Ukraine should not be divided by Russia.
items.title: Zelenskyy Warns Trump's Proposed Deal Could Be Dangerous

items.summary: Mogadishu residents reacted with mixed feelings after Somalia's Supreme Court ruled on Friday that President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term extension was unlawful. The opposition accuses the president of deploying troops to arrest the court's chief justice, claims AFP could not verify but which Somali media images reportedly support. The ruling follows disputes over constitutional amendments and comes amid a security crisis linked to Al-Shabaab as international donors cut funding.
items.title: Somalia Supreme Court ruling sparks political crisis over president's term extension

items.summary: Tokyo is considering paying its 2027 contributions to the International Criminal Court ahead of schedule, government sources said, in response to U.S. sanctions on the court. A Japanese official warned Friday that without action the ICC could face a funding shortfall. The ICC's 2026 budget totals about €196 million, or about ¥34.5 billion, and Japan contributed about ¥4.6 billion this year as its largest donor. Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said Thursday Tokyo would consider financial measures while communicating with President Tomoko Akane.
items.title: Japan Weighs Early ICC Contribution Amid U.S. Sanctions

items.summary: The mythological film Ramayana has drawn praise for Yash's portrayal of Ravana, who many viewers and director Dolly call a show-stealer. The movie opened to strong response and collected Rs 180 crore at the box office. Producer Abhishek Agarwal instead highlighted Ranbir Kapoor's transformation as Lord Rama, while both he and director Nitesh Tiwari urged avoiding comparisons with Ramanand Sagar's classic Ramayan.
items.title: Yash Praised as Ramayana's Biggest Talking Point Over Ranbir Kapoor

items.summary: Hyderabad-based Minorities Welfare Minister Mohammad Azharuddin backed Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's demand that he be allowed to speak in Parliament, saying discussions on the issue were welcome and noting Gandhi had long sought a debate. Azharuddin told ANI that while discussion could happen anywhere, parliamentary access was important. Separately, Union Minister Pralhad Joshi accused Gandhi of doing no homework on electoral roll revisions amid the row.
items.title: Minorities Minister Backs Congress Leader's Demand for Parliamentary Debate

items.summary: Human rights activist and 2023 Nobel Peace Prize winner Narges Mohammadi, interviewed by EL PAÍS from a Tehran prison video room while awaiting an 18-year sentence suspended in May after two heart attacks, describes the prize as having intensified pressure on her. She recounts being detained at least 14 times and tried 10 times, accumulating 44 years’ imprisonment and 154 lashes plus 161 days of solitary confinement since writing her memoir from Evin prison. Calling isolation “one of the Islamic Republic’s main instruments of torture,” she links it to coerced confessions and rising executions—citing Amnesty International’s estimate that around 4,500 people were executed in Iran alone during summer 1988—and credits women-led movements for advancing rights at high cost. She warns war with Israel and the United States has made the regime more repressive while she continues to hope to see her twins again one day.
items.title: Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi defends Iran’s resistance amid renewed repression

items.summary: Juan Manuel Santos, former president of Colombia (2010-2018), is the subject of an EL PAÍS profile built from four interviews conducted between April and September 2025. The piece opens with his January 2025 appearance before the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists, where he watched the Doomsday Clock sit at 89 seconds to midnight in 2025 and move closer — to 85 seconds away — by January 2026. Santos frames himself as a lifelong negotiator whose career moved from defense minister under Álvaro Uribe (2006-2009) to architect of the peace agreement with the FARC, signed in 2016 after more than 50 years of war. Ten years later he marks that anniversary while acknowledging its non-implementation and today's gang-driven violence. He attributes current global conflict partly to lost moderation and social media polarization, yet insists conflicts remain solvable: 'It's simply a matter of sitting down and talking.' The interviews were shaped by the June 2025 election victory and swearing-in of Abelardo de la Espriella, whose display of corpses after a military operation prompted Santos to reflect on state legitimacy. Attribution throughout carries uncertainty — many claims are his own interpretations rather than verified fact — while figures like the clock's setting remain stated flatly by the Bulletin.
items.title: Former Colombian President Reflects on Peace and a Fraying World

items.summary: Sucdi Abdul Fattah Abdul Khader, a 23-year-old Somali woman, guides visitors to Jazeera beach, sand dunes, the fish market and historic sites in an effort to reshape how the world sees Mogadishu. She works alongside her father, who guided for over three decades, and reaches wider audiences through TikTok videos of her tours. Sucdi says many tourists arrive expecting insecurity but are surprised by the country's beauty and welcoming people. Somalia's tourism department reported about 10,000 tourists visited in 2024, a 50% increase on the previous year, though she notes numbers remain low with five visitors a week considered success. Sucdi says her goal is to show landscapes, culture and people beyond negative headlines.
items.title: Somali tour guide reimagines Mogadishu beyond its headlines

items.summary: Actress Alia Bhatt shared pictures from her daughter Raha Kapoor's fourth birthday celebration on November 6. While the family moments drew attention, focus also turned to Alia's outfit: a floral Mirabel dress by Summer Away priced at Rs 8,720 per the brand's official website. Made of viscose georgette with a V-neckline and mini-length silhouette, it was styled understatedly for the event.
items.title: Alia Bhatt Wears ₹8,720 Floral Dress At Daughter Raha's Birthday

items.summary: Officials said on Saturday that Harry Boxer, a key operative of the wanted Lawrence Bishnoi gang, has been detained in the United States. American authorities apprehended him from California after inputs from Delhi Police's Special Cell and Haryana Police STF. He is linked to Rohit Shetty's February firing and other cases; Indian agencies are expected to seek his extradition with CBI assistance.
items.title: US Detains Lawrence Bishnoi Gang Operative Harry Boxer for Return to India

items.summary: Ahead of Diwali, Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration suspended 105 food business licences across the state during a special drive on November 4 and 5. The action included suspensions in Mumbai alone (28) and shutdown orders for outlets such as Rajdhani Biryani Centre. Suspected unsafe or adulterated stock worth over Rs 1.35 crore was seized from more than 69 establishments, despite prior warnings to vendors.
items.title: Maharashtra FDA Suspends Licences of Quick-Commerce and Food-Franchise Firms Ahead of Diwali

items.summary: A London-based commentator weighs in on repeated tech-stock shakeouts, asking whether the AI bubble is finally bursting or just another head fake. He notes that AI assets dominate markets and show hallmarks of an unsustainable boom, citing Bank for International Settlements figures that nearly 29 per cent of AI firms’ investment deals are with other AI firms. Markets briefly rose after Democratic midterm wins but fell sharply when voters rejected data centres; the Nasdaq Composite dropped 5 per cent on Thursday (Nov 5), its biggest fall in 19 months, while CoreWeave stocks fell 10 per cent and Sandisk 22 per cent. Trevor Greetham of Royal London Asset Management called the AI trade a shark that must keep swimming to stay alive.
items.title: Commentator Questions Whether AI Stock Bubble Is Bursting

items.summary: A survey invites school leaders, teachers, and parents to describe their experiences with artificial intelligence tools in communication between families and schools. It asks respondents whether they have received or written AI-generated emails, what impact those messages had on tone and quality, and whether the technology has eased contact or created new problems. The request notes that people having trouble completing the form can click a link for help.
items.title: Schools and parents invited to share AI email experiences

items.summary: Officials across Europe reported a fresh wave of bomb threats against multiple flights on Friday, November 6, following a string of hoaxes that caused flight diversions this week. The threats may be spreading beyond aviation: two broadcasters also received security warnings. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi covered the developing situation.
items.title: European Aviation Disrupted by Fresh Bomb Threats on Friday

items.summary: A Washington State judge approved a settlement in In re Amazon Return Policy Litigation for $309.5 million, payable to class members who bought physical items between September 5, 2017 and February 12, 2026, requested refunds that were never issued or were reversed after return. The lawsuit alleged Amazon failed to process compliant returns due to refund-process defects. Jeff Bezos' Amazon stated it is not involved in wrongdoing but agreed to avoid further litigation; the notice noted it does not express a court opinion on the merits.
items.title: Amazon Agrees to $309.5 Million Return Refund Settlement

items.summary: A report by Cease in the UK and Collective Shout in Australia accuses TikTok of helping promote and normalise the sex industry, according to a report. Researchers studied non-explicit posts over a year from some OnlyFans’ most popular young female performers, finding coded references hidden inside lifestyle content about shopping, pets or skincare. Performers reportedly used euphemisms like “corn” for porn or emoji combinations to evade blocks while hinting their adult content is available elsewhere. The report’s authors called for extending bans on explicit material shown to under-18s to include such promotional posts. Melinda Tankard Reist of Collective Shout condemned TikTok as an industrial-scale digital pimp grooming young women into producing explicit content, though the platform and OnlyFans both denied facilitating minors’ access.
items.title: Campaigners accuse TikTok of funneling girls into sex work

items.summary: Elon Musk announced on Friday that Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production around mid-2027 at its facility outside Austin, Texas. The move will free capacity for the company's Cybercab robotaxi as Tesla shifts focus toward autonomous vehicles. Contributing factors include disappointing sales and pricing: Kelley Blue Book estimated 20,237 units sold last year, roughly half of the prior year, with a further 28% decline through September this year versus Musk's projected annual target of 250,000 Cybertrucks. The promised price below $40,000 never materialised; early vehicles sold for double that or more. Growing controversy around Musk and his political associations also alienated some owners. Despite the shutdown, owner Ross Blankenship said he would buy another in a heartbeat, calling its end 'a sad moment.'
items.title: Tesla Winds Down Cybertruck Production in Mid-2027

items.summary: Donald Harrison, a SpaceX board member since 2015, resigned after more than a decade with the company. Bloomberg reported that independent directors are reportedly examining a potential merger between Elon Musk's SpaceX and Tesla, including special committees to assess a possible combination. No definitive agreement has been disclosed; efforts may target announcement in early next year.
items.title: SpaceX Board Member Donald Harrison Resigns Amid Tesla Merger Reports

items.summary: Engineers tested the world's first 4,000-meter-class airborne wind power system over Yueyang in central China on November 6. The China-made S4000 uses a helium-filled platform to lift power modules up to 4,000 meters and transmit electricity via tether cable. Officials say urban testing assesses safe operation near populated areas as cities become key deployment targets for high-altitude wind energy.
items.title: China Tests World's First High-Altitude Floating Wind Power System Over City

items.summary: Ayodhya celebrated its 10th Deepotsav festival along the Saryu River, with millions of earthen lamps illuminating more than 30 lakh lamps across 56 ghats. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan, Uttar Pradesh governor Anandiben Patel and chief minister Yogi Adityanath attended prayers before a gathering at Ram Katha Park. Adityanath called the event a symbol of Ayodhya's transformation following the Ram temple inauguration, while Patel highlighted rising tourism bringing economic opportunities to local residents.
items.title: Ayodhya lights up for Deepotsav on Diwali eve

items.summary: At the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit's forum on the Development of Internet Public Welfare, CGTN spoke with Chinese actor Yue Man-lok. He has sponsored children in rural China for years and described how the internet transformed charitable giving: supporting a cause no longer requires being there in person. "It's about how much you want to help," he said.
items.title: Yue Man-lok on How Internet Simplifies Charity Giving

items.summary: Congress Parliamentary party chairperson Sonia Gandhi said publisher Penguin Random House India was 'uneasy' with criticism of the government, in her first reaction to a controversy over an upcoming memoir titled Belonging: A Journey of Love. In the same statement she criticised shrinking space for opposition voices under the NDA government. The report is by Aastha Jha of The Times of India.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Says Penguin Was Uneasy Over Memoir Criticism

items.summary: Divi's Laboratories reported a 64% year-on-year rise in profit after tax, reaching Rs 1,127 crore for the quarter ended September 30. Net revenue from operations climbed 35.4% to Rs 3,676 crore, up from Rs 2,715 crore a year earlier. Consolidated total income rose to Rs 3,770 crore, while standalone first-half income reached Rs 6,765 crore against Rs 5,282 crore last year. The company's shares closed at Rs 10,305 on the BSE. Article author Kumar Gaurav disclosed no financial interest in the companies covered.
items.title: Divi's Laboratories Posts Strong Q2 Profit and Revenue Growth

items.summary: Rail minister Peter Hendy told a London industry conference this week that the legislation creating Great British Railways had “a fair chance of getting royal assent” before parliament’s winter break, potentially wrapping up its establishment in law by Christmas. The new arm’s-length body would bring track and train services under one control. Speakers acknowledged substantial challenges: network manager Network Rail cited two derailments within 24 hours amid a summer of delays, while the regulator Office of Rail and Road noted renewal spending had fallen from nearly £5bn to less than £4bn over five years. Some critics warned that future funding could remain uncertain under different governments.
items.title: Great British Railways law may pass by Christmas amid old problems

items.summary: German chancellor Friedrich Merz, Dutch prime minister Rob Jetten and four other European leaders wrote to Ursula von der Leyen and António Costa urging the UK’s return to the EU internal electricity market ahead of a 20 November summit. They argue integration would unlock North Sea clean energy and lower costs for British consumers. Officials warn it could be controversial, as the UK might contribute to cohesion funds.
items.title: Five European leaders urge closer EU-UK energy ties

items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky said overnight drone and ballistic missile attacks damaged Ukrainian energy infrastructure, causing blackouts and disrupting water supplies. He reported 12 regions came under attack with Kyiv hit hardest, nine people hurt including one child, and strikes on substations linking the Rivne and Khmelnytsky nuclear power plants to Kyiv.
items.title: Zelensky Reports Widespread Damage After Russian Strikes on Ukraine's Power Grid

items.summary: Two teenagers were arrested overnight and on Saturday morning after a suspected sword attack near St Peter's high school in Tuffley, Gloucester. A 17-year-old was reported with a superficial wound believed to have been caused by the sword; another 17-year-old boy was not physically injured. Officers responded shortly after 8.50am on Friday and armed police searched for suspects while schools were put on lockdown.
items.title: Two men arrested after boy injured in Gloucester sword attack

items.summary: As ballots from Tuesday's US midterm elections are still being counted, analysts pivot attention to the upcoming 2028 presidential contest. The article offers four takeaways: midterms winners now carry momentum, with Democrats buoyed by congressional gains; however, a strong showing does not guarantee victory two years later, as Barack Obama won in 2012 despite Republican midterm surges. Leadership figures like JD Vance and Marco Rubio face pressure amid voter anger over the administration, while left- and moderate-wing Democrats compete for influence. Hispanic voters' support must be actively earned by both parties as traditional strongholds shift.
items.title: Four Takeaways on the Shifting 2028 White House Race

items.summary: Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi took pole position for the Qatar Grand Prix on Saturday, Nov 7, smashing the lap record twice at Lusail. He clocked one minute 50.028 seconds, finishing 0.266 seconds ahead of championship leader Marc Marquez. Qualifying left only 18 riders on the grid after Yamaha teams withdrew over travel restrictions.
items.title: Bezzecchi smashes lap record twice to grab Qatar MotoGP pole from Marquez

items.summary: A single-sentence cartoon caption attributes a warning about dangerous technology innovations to Steve Jones, without further context or explanation of the subject's remarks. The item offers no figures, sources, or supporting detail beyond this one line.
items.title: Steve Jones Cartoon Warns Against Risky Technology Advances

items.summary: Moscow launched a massive overnight strike on Kyiv while Ukraine prepares for talks with Russia and the United States next week. At least five people were injured, and Russian missiles damaged buildings, closed a bridge over the Dnipro River, and caused power and water outages.
items.title: Russia Launches Massive Overnight Strike on Kyiv as Talks Loom

items.summary: After retiring from professional tennis in October, ending a 22-year career, Gael Monfils has become the captain of France's Davis Cup team, the French Tennis Federation (FFT) announced on Saturday. He took over the non-playing role from Paul-Henri Mathieu and is set to support France as they begin their qualifying campaign in February.
items.title: Gael Monfils becomes captain of France's Davis Cup team

items.summary: A company behind a large AI development near Glasgow has said the scheme will be fully served by the National Grid, revising an earlier pledge to draw 1GW from green sources. The Guardian prompted the change after questioning the commitment. DataVita says its grid supply would come through a renewable power purchase agreement and that solar and windfarms could connect later. It remains eligible for £202m in public wealth guarantees while planning a 500MW datacentre expected to create 3,400 jobs.
items.title: DataVita abandons renewable promise for Glasgow AI datacentre

items.summary: Researchers document that dengue-carrying Aedes aegypti mosquitoes have expanded across Nepal, reaching elevations up to 2,500 meters (8,200 feet) over the past decade. According to a January literature review in Clinical Infection in Practice, transmission has grown from localized outbreaks since first appearing in 2004 into major nationwide epidemics through 2019, 2022 and 2023. Local media report the virus reached 76 out of the country's 77 districts with roughly 9,000 recorded infections and at least six deaths in 2025 alone. Sunita Baral of Nepal Health Research Council notes dengue was once confined to lowland Terai regions but now appears in Kathmandu. Rising temperatures let mosquitoes survive higher altitudes while urban water storage creates breeding grounds. Erin Mordecai of Stanford University says global dengue burdens have risen roughly 18 percent over historical baselines, hitting cooler highlands hardest.
items.title: Dengue Fever Spreads Higher in Nepal's Warming Himalayas

items.summary: Sun coral, an invasive Indo-Pacific species first seen in Brazil in the 1980s, is spreading along roughly 3,500 kilometers (2,175 miles) of coastline. Estimates suggest it can expand at a rate of 2 kilometers (1.2 miles) per year and may alter reefs once it covers 45% of rocky substrate. In 2018 Brazil launched a National Plan to prevent, control and monitor the invasion. Marine biologist Adriana Gomes leads volunteer divers removing colonies near Cagarras Islands off Ipanema Beach.
items.title: Brazil Divers Remove Invasive Sun Coral Along Coastal Reefs

items.summary: Inside Climate News, via its partner Living on Earth, reports an interview with U.S. Rep. Jared Huffman, who is in line to chair the House Energy and Natural Resources Committee as Democrats take control. Huffman outlines a two-part agenda: oversight and investigations into matters like mineral deals involving Trump inner-circle financial interests and the Freedom 250 entity’s reprogrammed funds, plus an affirmative policy push he says must not be constrained by Donald Trump’s laws or permits. He cites rising utility bills and offshore wind cancellations as election drivers and flags a bipartisan Great American Outdoors Act 250 bill that Huffman hopes to advance in the lame duck session. Huffman notes subpoena power may come “sometime in January” and warns of two months of chaotic negotiations before the next Congress seats.
items.title: Huffman Vows Reset of Natural Resources Committee Agenda

items.summary: Mongabay reporter Max Radwin investigated illegal gold mining advancing on Indigenous Wayana communities in Suriname's Amazon, near the French Guiana border. Miners are clearing forest and polluting rivers with mercury despite a government pledge to combat the activity. The report directs readers to Mongabay's full story for more of his findings.
items.title: Illegal Gold Mining Expands Across Suriname's Indigenous Amazon Territory

items.summary: The company behind the under-construction Brenner Base Tunnel project, a 55 km rail link between Innsbruck in Austria and Fortezza in Italy, confirmed it had been hit by a cyberattack on 17 October after activating its security protocols. Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said he was targeted over Italy's support for Ukraine, with criminals sharing his personal data online; Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expressed her support. Initial investigations point to the pro-Russian group Everest, per Tiroler Tageszeitung.
items.title: Italian Foreign Minister and Tunnel Firm Hit by Cyberattacks

items.summary: Caregivers face a growing crisis as an estimated 63 million Americans cared for someone with a medical condition or disability in 2025, spending up to 27 hours per week on care. New caregiver apps are emerging to help manage medications, appointments, and communication between family members. Developers like Bret Koncak of Mejo and Nasha Fitter of Citizen Health aim to reduce the mental load by consolidating medical information and offering AI assistance. However, experts caution that most of these tools are not FDA-reviewed medical devices, their safety remains uncertain, and health data may fall outside HIPAA protections. One expert noted the solution requires collaboration across government, private sector, and families.
items.title: AI Caregiver Apps Promise Relief Amid Growing Burden

items.summary: A controversy has emerged around Miss Universe India 2026 after second runner-up Anushri Satavlekar relinquished her position and alleged the pageant's internal practices conflicted with her values. She claimed the crown was sold and the outcome had been planned, per a NewsX Live report. Nikhil Anand, National Director of Miss India Universe and chairman of Glam Anand Group, has reportedly sought clarification from Satavlekar over the allegations. The claims remain unverified in available information.
items.title: Miss Universe India contestant alleges pageant was planned, director seeks clarification

items.summary: Bookish Review examines Devki Pande’s debut novel, The Imitation Englishman (Bloomsbury India), which offers a fresh perspective on lesser-known strands of India’s freedom struggle. Set mostly in Europe and London around 1916, the story follows 20-year-old Madhusudan heading to Heidelberg University while his brother serves as a sepoy in North Africa during the First World War. Through his friendship with Amir Farooqui, involved in the Hindu-German conspiracy, Madhusudan learns about revolutionary activity and the freedom movement at home. Pande traces social history rather than popular hagiographies, showing the struggle comprised armed revolts, collaborators and quiet subversives. The reviewer notes the plot lacks cohesion and reads as two separate stories, though it remains a fast-paced read released in October amid national protests referencing India’s freedom struggle.
items.title: Review of The Imitation Englishman by Devki Pande

items.summary:
N Chandrababu Naidu's official residence at 1, Janpath Road in New Delhi was renovated at a cost of ₹6.5 crore, reported Indian Express. The restoration, carried out by NBCC (India) Ltd over three-and-a-half months and completed on October 22, upgraded the nearly 100-year-old bungalow while preserving its architectural design and heritage elements dating to the 1930s. NBCC said it reinforced the structure through retrofitting and added modern interiors, sustainable net-zero concepts and landscaped green spaces. Naidu held housewarming rituals there in July 2024 after his election as Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister, and has used the residence for official engagements with Union Ministers. The article also reports that he later visited cyclone-hit areas of Bapatla district to assess crop losses from Cyclone Murusu.

visual null},
items.title: Andhra Pradesh CM's Delhi Residence Renovated for ₹6.5 Crore

items.summary: The Indian Express reported that Mercury Public Affairs disclosed in a Foreign Agents Registration Act filing that a June social media post by President Donald Trump congratulating Prime Minister Narendra Modi was among tasks done for the Indian embassy’s monthly $75,000 retainer. Congress Media Coordinator Harmeet Kaur questioned what taxpayers receive from the government’s reported $225,000-a-month American lobbying spend.
items.title: Indian embassy lobbying retainer surfaces Trump congratulatory post

items.summary: Sonam Wangchuk has appealed to President Droupadi Murmu for urgent intervention, alleging that the Lieutenant Governor-led administration is running a targeted campaign to defame him and other critics. The appeal comes amid administrative action against institutions linked to him, including cancellation of Himalayan Institute of Alternatives' land lease in August 2025. Wangchuk released excerpts from what he called a sting operation implicating links with Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena's team. He also alleged restrictions on democratic rights and claimed liquor policy changes reduced mandatory No Objection Certificates from 16 to six, per PTI. The L-G's office gave no immediate response.
items.title: Climate Activist Appeals to President Over Alleged Smear Campaign in Ladakh

items.summary: Ayodhya's Deepotsav festival is set to light nearly 30 lakh traditional earthen diyas, aiming for its ninth Guinness World Record. Student volunteers and community members prepare the lamps, while officials link the event to cultural ties with Ramayana literature and urban development promoted by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath across Uttar Pradesh.
items.title: Ayodhya Lights Nearly 30 Lakh Diyas for Ninth World Record

items.summary: The US military carried out new airstrikes on Iranian air defence systems in southern Iran, targeting an anti-aircraft device on Qeshm Island. President Donald Trump called them “minor strikes,” saying the system was knocked out in about 15 minutes, maybe five, while insisting progress continues with Qatar’s mediation. Iranian state media reported two missiles hit Suza without identifying targets or damage; locals posted explosions online. The IRGC claimed to shoot down a US drone, which Washington did not confirm. Iran is reviewing Qatari proposals but remains unwilling to negotiate until core conditions are met: ending the port blockade, lifting sanctions, unfreezing assets and compensation. Diplomats across the Gulf stressed talks continue amid fears of an all-out war.
items.title: US Strikes Iranian Air Defenses as Diplomacy Continues

items.summary: The 2026 Global Mayors Dialogue opened in Ningbo on China's east coast, drawing mayors and representatives from 20 cities across 15 countries and regions. Participants discussed sustainable development through port trade cooperation, smart manufacturing, and urban governance. The event is organized by the host city as part of an international exchange among municipal leaders.
items.title: Mayors Gather in Ningbo for Global Dialogue

items.summary: Zhao Leji, chairman of the Standing Committee of China's National People's Congress, met separately with Gabonese President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema and Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker in Beijing on Friday. Zhao pledged to strengthen bilateral relations and expand cooperation with both countries, while each leader expressed hope for deeper legislative exchanges and closer ties.
items.title: China's top legislator meets Gabonese and Austrian leaders in Beijing

items.summary: Electric truck maker Harbinger raised $240 million in its latest Series D round, co-led by Tiger Global, the Capricorn Technology Impact Fund, and Ridgeline. The company says it will use the money to expand energy storage systems, power generation, autonomy software, defense applications, and medium-duty manufacturing capacity. Since 2021, Harbinger has raised over $650 million total. Co-Founder and CEO John Harris said electrification is central to its mission of reinventing critical systems.
items.title: Harbinger Secures $240 Million in Series D Funding Round

items.summary: Researchers using Chile's Very Large Telescope spotted a white dwarf, J1328−1450 in Virgo about 1,600 light-years away, whose debris disc forms two distinct rings rather than the single disc seen in the 21 similar systems previously found. Astronomer Felipe Lagos-Vilches said the configuration suggests planetary remnants can survive a star's transformation and may mirror our own solar system billions of years from now.
items.title: Astronomers Spot White Dwarf With Two Rings of Planetary Debris

items.summary: President Trump announced that NASA will launch its first nuclear-powered spacecraft, the Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom mission, to Mars within two years. Speaking at the UP Summit in Florida, he cited a Fox News report and linked the effort to his American Declaration of Freedom in Space. The reactor would power electric thrusters for deep-space travel.
items.title: Trump Sets Two-Year Deadline for NASA Nuclear Mars Mission

items.summary: Police say a 15-year-old boy killed his 58-year-old father at their home in Loni early Saturday after being scolded for fighting with his younger sister. The incident occurred between 2am and 3am while the family slept, according to police. ACP Ram Kishan of Loni Circle told HT that the boy attacked him with a sickle; other relatives then apprehended him and took him to a hospital where he was declared dead.
items.title: Teenager Kills Father After Being Scolded Over Fight With Sister in Loni

items.summary: Writer Perumal Murugan has accused the newly inaugurated Periyar Arivulagam library in Coimbatore of serious procurement irregularities, including AI-generated content, fictitious authors and inflated prices. In an article on Sindhai dated November 6, he counted nearly 1,800 books bearing the imprint of Agalvilakku Pathippagam and more than 100 titles from Phoenix Pathippagam. He cited a Rs 1,445 price tag versus comparable copies at approximately Rs 350, plus historical errors such as misattributing Naladiyar to an individual poet. Tamil Nadu School Education Minister A Rajmohan said about 1,500 books were purchased during the previous DMK administration and filed a complaint with DVAC on November 7. The ruling TVK blames the former DMK government; both parties demand investigations as the outcome remains awaited.
items.title: Tamil Writer Accuses Coimbatore Library of AI-Generated Books and Fake Authors

items.summary: A former regional business head of Tech Mahindra’s Asia-Pacific region, Paramjith Dhankhar, was shot dead on Friday night by his neighbour Mohan Sharma over a parking dispute that had strained the two families for days. The feud also involved Sharma’s son allegedly using his dog to defecate in the shared area. Police said nine of at least 15 fired bullets hit Dhankhar, whose body went to Badshah Khan Civil Hospital for autopsy; Sharma has since been arrested (PTI).
items.title: Neighbour Shoots Former Tech Mahindra Executive Over Parking Feud in Faridabad

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended Diwali greetings on Saturday, describing the festival as symbolising India's determination to overcome darkness. He reaffirmed his annual tradition of celebrating with armed forces personnel, a practice he has followed for years. In a video message shared on X, he wished citizens happiness, peace and prosperity, while also greeting Vice-President CP Radhakrishnan earlier that day.
items.title: PM Modi Extends Diwali Greetings and Vows to Continue Tradition With Soldiers

items.summary: Congress chairperson Sonia Gandhi said publisher Penguin Random House India declined her memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love because it was uneasy with criticism of the government. She called the refusal an attempt to censor her book and described being disappointed but not surprised. The Guardian reported her comments ahead of a November 10 release; HarperCollins India then agreed to publish it domestically that same day.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Blames Penguin for Memoir Withdrawal, Calls It Censorship

items.summary: Yamaha is expanding its electric scooter range with the XENTER E, a high-wheel 16-inch model aimed at European city riding. It uses Yamaha's new eAxle powertrain producing 7.5 kW of peak power and places it in Europe's A1 license category. Powered by a 3.5 kWh battery claiming 108 km on the WMTC Class 1 cycle, early reports point to €7,799 in Germany, with deliveries expected from spring 2027.
items.title: Yamaha Unveils High-Wheel Electric Scooter Targeting European Commuters

items.summary: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) warned Saturday that heavy rains have flooded shelters in the Gaza Strip, placing displaced families at 'immediate risk.' OCHA said most of Gaza's 2.1 million residents remain displaced and living in deteriorating tents with limited protection against worsening weather. The agency described emergency supplies as 'insufficient,' citing months of funding shortfalls and restrictions that constrained preparations, and urged the immediate entry of winter materials plus additional funding.
items.title: OCHA warns Gaza flood victims face immediate risk amid supply shortages

items.summary: Democratic lawmakers across Europe are urging stricter regulation of AI data centres, a stance echoed continent-wide. In Amsterdam, hundreds of activists occupied the site where a planned Microsoft facility was to be built during a two-day protest spanning the region.
items.title: European Democrats Push Back on AI Data Centres Amid Protests

items.summary: BBT SE, which operates the Brenner Base Tunnel linking Austria and Italy, confirmed a cyberattack to Tiroler Tageszeitung on 07 November 2026. Local media reports suggest the Russian-speaking group Everest may be responsible, citing links to an international extortion network; ZeroFox analysis describes such groups as stealing data and demanding payment. The company said it isolated affected systems, notified authorities, and found no operational impact.
items.title: Brenner Base Tunnel Operator Hit by Suspected Russian Cyberattack

items.summary: Websol Energy System reported second-quarter FY27 results via an exchange filing. Revenue from operations rose 114.6% YoY to Rs 361.02 crore in Q2FY27 against Rs 168.22 crore a year earlier, and EBITDA climbed 77.3% to Rs 128.14 crore from Rs 72.29 crore. Cell production reached 255 MW at 91% utilisation, module output was 88 MW at 68%, and the order book stood at Rs 1,280 crore as of September 30, 2026. Managing Director Sohan Lal Agarwal said the quarter showed manufacturing progress while preparing for expansion into EPC, solar IPP and energy trading.
items.title: Websol Energy Q2 Results: PAT jumps 73% YoY to Rs 80 crore; revenue more than doubles to Rs 361 crore

items.summary: Russian authorities said Russia launched overnight strikes on Kyiv, hitting the Northern Bridge and Meridian Plant, which they say produce Flamingo cruise missiles. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy attributed 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles to Russia, calling it an attempt to force a blackout. Ukrainian officials confirmed damage and one death; the attacks come days before trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi.
items.title: Russia strikes Kyiv with drones and missiles ahead of talks

items.summary: Bitcoin and Ethereum gained roughly 0.6% and 0.8% over the past 24 hours, while BNB, Solana, Hyperliquid, Dogecoin and Cardano rose up to 1.8%. ZebPay's Harish Vatnani said crypto stayed under pressure after the Binance security incident, heavy ETF outflows and a US tech sell-off outweighed a post-election rally; sentiment swung back into fear as the Fear & Greed Index fell from 50 to 28 and market capitalisation slipped to about $2.6 trillion. BTC is now about 40% below its October all-time high of around $126,000 and trades just above the $75,000 support level.
items.title: Crypto Markets Rise as Jobs Data Weighs on Bitcoin

items.summary: U.S. solar equipment inventories expanded by 126% during the second quarter of 2026 as project developers accelerated procurement ahead of federal trade cutoffs, including a July construction-start deadline and Dec. 4 measures affecting polysilicon, wafers, cells, and modules. OCI Energy CEO Sabah Bayatli said uncertainty over minimum import price thresholds—$0.22 per watt for cells and $0.38 per watt for finished modules—makes pricing difficult post-December. Developers are restructuring multi-party contracts to share tariff risk rather than speculating on spot prices, with costs ultimately flowing into higher power purchase agreement pricing.
items.title: U.S. solar developers brace for Section 232 tariff deadline

items.summary: Women in Solar+ Europe (WiSEu) explored how diverse teams can improve decisions during six Solar & Storage Live events across the UK, Spain, Switzerland, Italy and France this year. The article reports that trust, participation and leadership enable people to challenge assumptions, shape outcomes and take ownership without senior titles. Quotes from Carmen Madrid of Women in Solar+ Europe, Jessimiela Usidame, Kim Keats Martínez, Filipa Monteiro Martins, Hollie Carek and Nadia Lalout-Landemaine support the argument. The piece notes that silence locks in risk and cost, and calls for everyday inclusive practices ahead of a WiSEu Breakfast Workshop on 25 November during Genera in Madrid.
items.title: How the Solar+ industries can make better decisions for the energy transition

items.summary: Partial results from South Africa's local elections suggest coalition battles in several major cities as the once-dominant ANC is set to lose significant support, with nearly 31% of votes out of 90% counted. The DA has gained ground but remains short of its 2016 peak, while MK is contesting for the first time since forming in 2023 and may finish third nationally. Analyst Daniel Silke told AFP that complex negotiations lie ahead as parties bargain to assemble governing alliances.
items.title: South African Local Elections Point to Coalition Battles

items.summary: A reference lists Diwali 2026 as falling on Sunday, November 8. Citing Drik Panchang, it gives the New Delhi Lakshmi Puja muhurat from 5:54 PM to 7:50 PM, an auspicious window of about one hour and 56 minutes during Vrishabha Kaal. The timings may vary across cities depending on local sunset and Panchang calculations.
items.title: Diwali 2026 Lakshmi Puja Timings Listed for Major Indian Cities
